chunks: From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Jameela, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for one of her needs, so he said to her: 'Perhaps you are from the Musawwifaat (women who delay).' She said, 'And what are the Musawwifaat, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The woman whose husband calls her for one of his needs, but she does not cease to delay him until her husband becomes drowsy and sleeps. That is the one whom the Angels do not cease cursing until her husband wakes up.'

key_terms.الْمُسَوِّفَاتُ: Women who delay or procrastinate, specifically in the context of marital relations or needs.
key_terms.تَلْعَنُهَا: Curses her (invokes divine displeasure upon her).

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Musawwifa' in Shia hadith and what is its spiritual consequence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identified the 'al-Musawwifa' as a woman who deliberately delays responding to her husband's call for his needs until he becomes drowsy and falls asleep. This specific act of neglect is cited as a cause for continuous cursing by the Angels until the husband awakens, highlighting the spiritual consequences of marital inattention. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on mutual responsiveness and the fulfillment of conjugal rights as a means of maintaining spiritual harmony within the household.
